Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Namibia has a partially deployed national identity system. The National Population Registration System (NPRS) is fully operational and issues physical national ID cards with biometrics (photo and 10-fingerprint) nationwide. However, the new e-ID (electronic/digital ID card with microchip) is planned for launch in July 2026 and has not yet been deployed. The Civil Registration and Identification Act 2024 (Act 13 of 2024) was gazetted but is not yet in force. The country scores 4 (partially deployed) as the physical ID system with digital backend is nationwide but the e-ID/digital credential is not yet operational.
